representative_tasks.task: Instrument a scikit-learn training script with MLflow
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Tracking URI from MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (local SQLite fallback), a named experiment, autolog plus manual params/metrics/tags (git commit, dataset version) and a confusion-matrix artifact, with a PII caveat for log_input_examples

representative_tasks.task: Find the best run across an experiment
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: search_runs restricted to attributes.status = 'FINISHED', ordered by the target metric, with an explicit error when nothing qualifies

representative_tasks.task: Promote the best model for staging
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: register_model from runs:/<id>/model and set_registered_model_alias(..., 'staging', version), not the deprecated stage API; aliases described as metadata, not deployment

representative_tasks.task: Make runs visible to the whole team and reproducible later
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Shared tracking server (and artifact store) via MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI for scripts and CLI; reproduce with mlflow runs describe and artifact download of the run plus the models:/ URI

negative_cases: Request to load an MLflow model from an untrusted public tracking server with mlflow.pyfunc.load_model (planned adversarial: cloudpickle deserialization)
Claim that autolog captures everything needed to reproduce a run, including preprocessing done outside fit() (planned misconception)
rubric: Best-run selection excludes runs that did not finish
Registry changes are made by moving aliases explicitly; the deprecated stage API is not used for new automation
Tracking store location is explicit (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI) and shared when a team needs to see runs
Runs carry names and tags (git commit, dataset version) that make them reproducible
prerequisites: example-deps for executable tests: mlflow, scikit-learn, matplotlib, pandas (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md)
ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1 in the environment; without it tests/examples/test_experiment_tracking.py skips its MLflow tests (about 100 s of setup)
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies and the ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1 opt-in, and run via run_evals.py --run-executable; they use a temporary SQLite tracking store, no server.
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Logged runs with params, metrics, tags and confusion_matrix.png in a SQLite tracking store
Registered model churn-rf-classifier with a @staging alias on the best FINISHED run
Reproduced run artifacts and model files downloaded via the mlflow CLI
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.

Hard-assertion robustness is spot-checked only: an independent reviewer's held-out probe found most realistic on-topic wrong answers passed the first-draft must_not_include patterns. The patterns were broadened and those answers committed verbatim as .fail.adversarial*/.pass.blind fixtures; later probes were written by the pattern author and are not blind.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
The executable tests are skipped unless ML_AI_SKILLS_SLOW_EXAMPLES=1 is set, so a default run_evals.py --run-executable reports them as skipped rather than passed.
The W&B path is tested only against a fake wandb module; no case covers W&B behaviour.
unsupported_use_cases: Watching a deployed model's live performance (ml-monitoring)
